description: Ad Infinitum 🚀 is a multidisciplinary team dedicated to decoding our planet's signals through satellite observation and continuous data analysis. Guided by boundless curiosity, we track environmental patterns to understand Earth's evolution and provide evidence-based answers.
summary:
We built an interactive website that shows how environmental variables have changed over time in each of the nine departments of San Luis, Argentina, a semiarid province where water is a key constraint. Users pick a department and a parameter, and get a chart with a clear conclusion: increase, decrease, or no significant change. Using NASA POWER data and satellite detections, we apply the Mann-Kendall test and Sen’s slope to separate real trends from natural variability, focusing on wildfires, water balance, and soil moisture.
The system is built to scale: more API parameters, derived variables (such as the Thornthwaite-Mather water balance), other problems, other regions worldwide, and future Machine Learning forecasting. The tool helps local authorities, farmers and communities detect long-term climate trends, anticipate drought and fire risk, and make better decisions on land and water management in a semi-arid region increasingly affected by climate variability.
details:
ECO-MONITOR: A Digital Tool for Trend Monitoring and Environmental Foresight

We have more environmental data than ever before, so why are we still reacting instead of preventing? Every landscape leaves behind clues about its future, are we reading them in time?

The satellite and reanalysis data describing variations in hydrological and weather trends already exist and are publicly available. The problem is that they come in complex technical formats, are difficult to interpret, and, above all, fail to answer the single question that matters to decision-makers: Is this actually changing, or was it just an unusual year?

Statistical Methods

To analyze the time series, we combine four complementary methods.

  • Mann-Kendall Test: Detects whether a statistically significant upward or downward trend exists. Because it is non-parametric, extreme years or outliers do not distort the long-term result.
  • Sen’s Slope: Quantifies the magnitude of the trend (rate of change per unit of time) using the median of pairwise slopes, maintaining resistance to outliers.

Scalability: How the Project Can Grow

Eco Forensic uses a modular pipeline that scales in four directions without rebuilding its core:

  • New Domains: Adding NASA POWER variables simply requires updating the query—expanding into frost risk, heat stress, or renewable energy potential.
  • Derived Indicators: Combining raw data into composite indices like the Thornthwaite-Mather water balance, drought indices (SPI/SPEI), and fire danger ratings.
  • Global Reach: Leveraging NASA POWER’s global coverage to scale beyond San Luis via dedicated server infrastructure.
  • ML Forecasting: Training machine learning models on clean historical series to project near-term climate scenarios with quantified uncertainty.

TECHNOLOGY USED

To develop Eco-Forensic, we combined:

  • Coding Languages & Frameworks: We used Python for the backend (data retrieval and statistical analysis) and JavaScript, TypeScript, and Next.js for the frontend interface.
  • AI Tools & Software: We integrated generative AI tools throughout the development lifecycle, using Gemini and ChatGPT for technical research, data analysis support, and code generation; Copilot for debugging and code review; and Claude Code for interface prototyping and component layout.
